title: ክብረ ነገሥት
draftNote: Geʿez as in HaCohen's Unicode text of Bezold (1905), checked against the printed page; translations original. The word-level romanization is generated mechanically and approximate; per-word glosses are best-effort — readers can suggest corrections with the ⚑ button.
titleEn: The Glory of Kings — God's Presence Everywhere (ch. 101)
source: Carl Bezold, Kebra Nagast: Die Herrlichkeit der Könige (Munich, 1905), ch. 101 — public domain. Geʿez text as in Ran HaCohen's Unicode edition of Bezold (tau.ac.il/~hacohen/KN, from Michal Jerabek's 1995 digitization), archived and checked against Bezold's printed page. Per-sign transliteration derived mechanically from Unicode; word-level romanization auto-generated (schwa-reduced) and approximate. Transliteration convention: ś = ሠ-series, ʿ = ዐ-series, ə = 6th order, 1st order ä, 4th order a. Translations made fresh from the Geʿez; Dillmann's Lexicon (1865) the lexical aid.
about: God, speaking in the first person, orders a first court to be made for her (the Ark, it seems), closed to the unclean and declares that he is present everywhere: with Daniel, Jonah, Joseph and Jeremiah, beneath the stacked layers of creation, above the heavens, with the Son and the Holy Spirit.

sentences.n: Chapter heading. ፻፩ is the numeral 101 (፻ = 100, ፩ = 1). በእንተ is 'concerning' (the usual heading formula); ህላዌ is a verbal noun of ሀሎ 'to be, exist' ('being, existence'), and ኵለሄ is 'everywhere' (ኵሉ 'all' + the place-ending -ሄ); the wording is close to 'concerning existence-everywhere'. The title is ours, not a manuscript's.

sentences.l: And-again he-said to-him: Make for-her a-court first, ዴዴ(?), that not may-enter there the-defiled and-unclean and-who-not he-is clean, for I I-will-be with-her, and-not there her-alone but where all her-likeness, where is-called my-name in-purity;
sentences.i: And again he said to him: Make for her a first court, ዴዴ (?), so that no one defiled or unclean may enter there, nor anyone who is not clean. For I will be with her, and not there with her alone, but wherever any likeness of her is, wherever my name is called upon in purity.
sentences.n: Start here: ወካዕበ is ወ- 'and' + ካዕበ 'again, a second time'; ይቤሎ is 'he said to him' (ይቤ 'he said' + -ሎ 'to him'), the standard way the text introduces a speaker, and what follows is God speaking in the first person; the addressee is not named in this part, and the speech seems to concern the dwelling being prepared for the Ark (ታቦት, feminine, hence ላቲ 'for her' and ኀቤሃ 'with her') (?). ግበር is the imperative 'make!'. ዴዴ I cannot identify (?): the same word stands after አነ in ch. 98, where it is left unplaced; here it follows ዐጸደ ቀዳሚ and context might suggest an adverb such as 'round about', but I have no lexical support, so it is left as printed. ዐጸደ ቀዳሚ is 'a first court' (ዐጸደ the accusative of ዐጸድ 'enclosure, court' with the adjective ቀዳሚ 'first'). ከመ ኢይባእ 'so that ... not enter' is the purpose pattern: ከመ + a subjunctive verb, here negated by ኢ-. ሥኡብ and ወርኩስ are adjectives of uncleanness ('defiled', 'unclean'; the sense of ሥኡብ is taken from context (?)); ዘኢኮነ ንጹሐ is a ዘ- relative, 'whoever is not clean' (ዘ- + ኢ- + ኮነ, the perfect of 'be', here a general statement; ንጹሐ is the accusative predicate 'clean'). እስመ 'for, because'; እሄሉ is the first-person subjunctive/imperfect of ሀሎ 'to be', 'I will be / I am to be'; ወአኮ 'and not'; ባሕቲታ 'her alone' (ባሕቲት 'alone' + the suffix -ኣ 'her', together -ታ), i.e. 'with her alone, by herself'; አምሳሊሃ 'her likeness' (አምሳል, singular as in ch. 55, + -ሃ 'her'; with ኵሉ, 'every likeness of her', perhaps the copies of the Ark (?)). ይጼዋዕ ስምየ is 'is called my name', i.e. 'my name is invoked'. The lexical calls here (ዴዴ above all) are hedged.

sentences.l: I-have-been with Daniel in the-pit, and-I-have-been with Jonah in the-belly-of the-great-fish, and-I-have-been with Joseph in the-pit, and-I-have-been with Jeremiah in the-well-of mire;
sentences.i: I was with Daniel in the pit, and I was with Jonah in the belly of the great fish, and I was with Joseph in the pit, and I was with Jeremiah in the well of mud.
sentences.n: Start here: ሀሎኩ is the perfect of ሀሎ 'to be, be present' in the first person singular, 'I was / I have been (present)' (ሀሎ is a stative verb, so its perfect can also serve as a present, 'I am'; I use 'I was' for these past rescues and 'I have been' in the units below); it is the refrain of the passage and begins nearly every unit below. ምስለ 'with', ውስተ 'in, into'. Four scriptural rescues are named: Daniel in the lions' den (Daniel 6), Jonah in the belly of the great fish (Jonah 1:17; ዐንበሪ is a large sea creature, here 'great fish'), Joseph in the pit (Genesis 37), and Jeremiah in the muddy cistern (Jeremiah 38:6). ግብ is the 'pit' or 'den' (used for both Daniel and Joseph). ከርሠ ዐንበሪ is a construct chain, 'belly-of (the) great-fish'; likewise ዐዘቅተ ዐምዐም 'well-of mire' (I take ዐምዐም as 'mud, mire' (?)). The third ሀሎኩ is spelled ወህሎኩ here, with ህ (sixth order) as the first sign instead of ሀ (first order); this looks like a spelling variant of the same verb, not a different word.

sentences.l: I-have-been I-support beneath the-below-of the-lowest, that not they-sink the-mountains beneath the-waters, and-I-have-been beneath the-waters, that not they-sink upon the-fire and ተይ; I-have-been I-support beneath the-fire and ተይ, that not they-sink above the-winds and ዛሕል; I-have-been beneath the-winds and ዛሕል, that not they-sink beneath the-darkness, and-beneath-it-too of-the-darkness and-of-the-deeps; I I-support, and-on-me leans all creation, and-me is-borne all that I-created;
sentences.i: I have been supporting them beneath the lowest of the low, so that the mountains do not sink beneath the waters; and I have been beneath the waters, so that they do not sink upon the fire and ተይ (?); I have been supporting beneath the fire and ተይ (?), so that they do not sink above the winds and ዛሕል (?); I have been beneath the winds and ዛሕል (?), so that they do not sink beneath the darkness, nor beneath the very underside of the darkness and of the deeps (?). I am the one who holds them up. All creation leans on me, and by me everything that I created is borne.
sentences.n: Start here: this is one long chain of stacked supports, each layer held up by God from beneath: mountains over waters, waters over fire, fire over winds, winds over darkness and the deeps. There is no ፤ inside it to cut at, so it stays one unit. ሀሎኩ አዐምድ is 'I have been (and am) supporting': ሀሎኩ + an imperfect verb; አዐምድ is 'I make stand / I prop up' (from ዐምድ 'pillar', so 'I act as a pillar') (?). መትሕተ and ታሕተ both mean 'beneath'; ታሕቲት is 'lowest' or 'lower part' ('beneath the below of the lowest'). ከመ ኢይሰጠሙ 'that they not sink' is ከመ + negative subjunctive, a purpose clause, with ይሰጠሙ 'they sink' (plural, subject the mountains/waters/etc.). ወተይ and ወዛሕል are crux words (?): I cannot identify ተይ or ዛሕል with confidence, and they may be names or terms for cosmic elements or levels; I leave them untranslated, and a printed or scribal corruption is possible (ተይ also stands beside fire in ch. 100, part 2: ወእሳት ወተይ). ወመትሕቴሃኒ ለጽልመት is 'and beneath it too, of the darkness': the suffix -ሃ 'it' anticipates its owner ጽልመት, which ለ- then names (compare አምሳሊሃ ለፀሐይ, ch. 55), and -ኒ is the emphatic 'also, even'; ወለቀላያት continues the same ለ- ('and of the deeps'), so I take both as further things beneath which nothing may sink, and አነ አዐምድ as a new clause 'I support'; the other reading, ለቀላያት as the object of አዐምድ ('I support the deeps'), is possible (?). ቀላያት is 'the deeps, the seas'. ያሰምክ 'it leans / is made to rest on' (from the root 'to lean, rest on'; the causative is used with ኀቤየ 'on me') (?). ይጸወን 'is borne, carried' (?): ኪያየ is an accusative pronoun, which a plain passive could not take, so this is a loose reading, and the verb may rather mean 'rests upon' with ኪያየ as its object (?). ዘፈጠርኩ is a ዘ- relative, 'that which I created', with ፈጠርኩ 'I created' as the first-person perfect (-ኩ).

sentences.n: Start here: ህሎኩ is again a spelling variant of ሀሎኩ 'I have been'. አጽናፈ ዓለም 'ends-of the-world' is a construct chain; I take አጽናፈ here as 'at the ends', an accusative of place (?). እሰፍን is 'I measure / extend' (?), the root can mean to measure out or to stretch; I choose 'measure' (if the verb were ሰፈረ 'measure', the form would be እሰፍር; a scribal ን for ር is possible (?)). ኵሎ is the accusative 'everything'.

sentences.i: I have been in the air, my dwelling place, and I have been above the chariot of the cherubim, praised always by all the angels and by holy men (?).
sentences.n: Start here: በአየር is በ- 'in' + አየር 'air'; ማኅደርየ is 'my dwelling' (ማኅደር + -የ 'my'). ሰረገላ ኪሩቤል 'chariot-of cherubim' is another construct chain, recalling Ezekiel's vision of the cherubim and wheels (Ezekiel 1 and 10) and the 'chariot of the cherubim' of 1 Chronicles 28:18 (?). እሴባሕ is 'I am praised' (a passive/reflexive stem, first person) (?), and ወትረ is 'always, continually'; እምኵሉ መላእክት is 'by all the angels' (እም- marking the agent after a passive), though 'more than all the angels' is also possible (?). The end is a crux (?): the text prints ወሰ ፡ ብእ with a space; I read it as ወሰብእ 'and men', so 'by all angels and holy men', but ወሰ ('and also') plus an odd ብእ is possible. ቅዱሳን 'holy ones' is the plural of ቅዱስ.

sentences.i: I exist in every place, and there is no other god besides me, in heaven above or on earth below.
sentences.n: Start here: ህልው is a participle/adjective 'existing, present', related to ሀሎ and to ህላዌ in the heading; with አነ 'I' it makes a verbless sentence, 'I am existing'. ዘእንበሌየ is 'besides me, without me' (ዘእንበለ + -የ). በላዕሉ and በታሕቱ are 'above (it)' and 'below (it)'; the suffix -ሁ 'its' is absorbed into the final consonant, giving -ሉ and -ቱ. The words recall Deuteronomy 4:39 and the commandment 'no other gods before me' (Exodus 20:3); I note the echo, not a quotation.

sentences.l: There-is-not what resembles me, said God;
sentences.i: There is none who is like me, said God.
sentences.n: Start here: ዘይመስል 'who resembles' (ዘ- relative + 'he resembles'); ኪያየ is the object form 'me' (ኪያ- + -የ), after 'resemble'. ይቤ እግዚኣብሔር is the quotation formula 'God said'; it appears inside the speech and names the speaker for the first time, so the 'he' of ይቤሎ above is God. Compare Isaiah 46:9 ('there is none like me'); the echo is general (?).

sentences.l: My-hand founded-her the-earth, and-my-right-hand made-firm-her the-heaven; I with my-son and-spirit holy.
sentences.i: My hand founded the earth, and my right hand made firm the heavens; I am with my Son and the Holy Spirit.
sentences.n: Start here: ሣረረታ is ሠረረት 'she founded' + -ኣ 'her' (the -ት is the 3fs subject, agreeing with feminine እዴየ 'my hand'; the -ኣ is the object 'her', ምድር being feminine too; ሣ for ሠ is a spelling variant (?)). The object suffix is doubled by ለምድር 'the earth' (ለ- marks the object here), a regular Geʿez way of marking a known object; likewise አጽንዐታ (አጽንዐት 'she made firm' + -ኣ 'her'; subject የማንየ, also feminine) ለሰማይ 'made-her-firm the heaven'. Compare Isaiah 48:13, where likewise the hand founds the earth and the right hand the heavens (the verbs are not the same). እዴየ 'my hand' and የማንየ 'my right hand' (የማን 'right') are the subjects. The last clause, 'I with my Son and the Holy Spirit', is a Trinitarian statement; the -የ in ወልድየ is 'my'. The part ends with the row of ፨ marks, which close the section and are attached to this last unit.
